messages:
maria: quick heads-up — i'm running terraform plan in staging after importing a k8s namespace and the plan keeps proposing a recreate of that namespace + apply stalls with a lock error. anyone seen intermittent dynamodb locks after imports?
eli: what backend are you using? s3 + dynamodb? can you paste the exact error from terraform? :eyes:
sarah: also which provider version for the k8s provider? provider schema changes often cause spurious diffs after import.
maria: yes s3+dynamodb. provider is kubernetes v2.11.0. plan error snippet:```
Error: Error locking state: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed
	status code: 400, request id: abc-123
```
then later when i try apply i get:```
Error: State snapshot was updated but remote state could not be locked: ConditionalCheckFailedException
```
darren: that CRUD. two quick things: (1) check dynamodb table for a stale lock item (it has the lock id as the key), (2) confirm the import didn't create metadata fields that the provider considers managed differently after the version change.
eli: to check locks quickly run:```
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name terraform-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"<lock-id>"}}' --region us-west-2
```
or list recent items:```
aws dynamodb scan --table-name terraform-locks --limit 20 --region us-west-2
```
if you see a lock item from your session that shouldn't be there, you can force-unlock:```
terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>
```
(note: only force-unlock if you're sure no other apply is running)
sarah: and for the recreate -- run `terraform state show kubernetes_namespace.xxx` and diff against `kubectl get ns <name> -o yaml`. provider 2.11 added handling for managedFields and some annotation normalization; the import may have pulled an older shape. I usually `terraform state replace-provider` or update the state to match the provider shape before planning.
maria: hmm i pulled state show and saw managed_fields present in the state which live cluster doesn't have (we scrubbed them during a migration). plan is comparing and wants to replace. any safe way to remove those from state?
darren: you can use `terraform state rm` then re-import with `terraform import` after adjusting the resource id mapping, but that's messy. alternative: use `terraform state replace-provider` only for provider name changes. For small diffs you can `terraform state show -no-color > s.txt` then edit and `terraform state push` (risky).
eli: another approach: add lifecycle ignore_changes for the problematic attributes (e.g., metadata[0].annotations or managed_fields) in the resource temporarily, run plan/apply, then remove the ignore afterward once state and cluster match. Example:```
resource "kubernetes_namespace" "app" {
  metadata {
    name = "app-namespace"
    # temporary to skip managed fields diff
    lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations, metadata[0].managed_fields] }
  }
}
```
maria: ok i'll try the ignore_changes route in a canary workspace. for the lock, i found an item in dynamodb with LockID = "tf-lock-2247654319" and owner = "apply-jenkins-3" but there are no running applies in jenkins. safe to force-unlock?
sarah: if jenkins isn't running and you confirmed no apply process, force-unlock. also check the aws request logs to ensure no network flakiness during the earlier apply.
terraform-bot: reminder — forcing unlock for tf state may break an in-progress apply. run `terraform force-unlock -force <LOCK_ID>` only when certain.
maria: did force-unlock, re-ran refresh then import again. plan is cleaner now but still shows a replace due to `metadata[0].managed_fields`. i'll add the lifecycle ignore, replan in staging, and post back. thanks all :raised_hands:
eli: if that works, do a quick postmortem note in #eng-infra about the provider version drift and we should pin staging provider to match prod to avoid surprises. :+1:
maria: will do, thanks!
